task_description: De novo design of synthetic hydrogels achieving robust underwater adhesion (>1 MPa) by statistically replicating sequence features of natural adhesive proteins
input: Protein sequence features converted to monomer compositions (6 monomer types: Nucleophilic-HEA, Hydrophobic-BA, Acidic-CBEA, Cationic-ATAC, Aromatic-PEA, Amide-AAm)
methodological_commitments: Machine learning-based optimization using RFR and GP models
Statistical replication of natural adhesive protein sequence features
Multi-round Bayesian optimization with Expected Improvement (EI) acquisition
required_artifacts: Data overview plots showing adhesive strength distributions
Correlation analysis between monomer compositions and adhesive strength
ML model performance comparison (R², RMSE, MAE)
comparison_structure: Performance tier analysis (Low <100 kPa, Medium 100-200 kPa, High >200 kPa)
ML method comparison (RFR-RFR, RFR-GP, GP-GP, GP-RFR, etc.)
interpretability_requirements: Feature importance from Random Forest and Gradient Boosting
